newsitem.title: CANADA: WIC to buy Videotron's CFCF-12.
newsitem.headline: WIC to buy Videotron's CFCF-12.

text.p: Groupe Videotron Ltee said on Friday that it agreed to sell the broadcasting operations of CFCF-12 to a joint-venture between WIC Western International Communications Ltd and Quebec's Caisse de depot et placement for a base price of C$70 million.
The base price is subject to certain working capital requirements and will be increased by up to C$30 million depending on CFCF-12s revenue stream over 1997 and 1998, Videotron said.
The joint-venture will be 70 percent held by WIC and 30 percent by the Caisse, Quebec's public pension fund manager.

The sale encompasses Montreal television station CFCF-12 and CFCF Inc's 14.2 percent participation in the CTV Television Network Ltd and is subject to various conditions precedent and regulatory approvals, Videotron said.

These include approval by the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (CRTC). The addition of up C$30 million to the C$70 million base price will be made only if within two years of the closing date the CRTC has not granted a license for an additional English-language television station serving all or part of the CFCF-12 extended market area of Montreal, Videotron said.
In a statement, WIC President and Chief Executive John Lacey said the CFCF-12 acquistion was a valuable opportunity to establish a presence in Quebec and expand the group nationwide.

If approved, the addition of CFCF-12 would mean that WIC's wholly owned WIC Televison would own and operate nine stations in Canada and increase its ownership in the CTV network to 28 percent from 14 percent, the company said.
The CFCF-12 broadcasting operations were acquired by Videotron earlier this year through its takeover of CFCF Inc .
